name: marketing-footers
title: Footers
description: Marketing website footer sections with navigation link columns, newsletter forms, social icons, branding, and copyright — in large multi-column, simple stacked, simple row, CTA-gradient, split, and slim styles.
useWhen: Closing every page of a marketing website with navigation links, legal text, and branding.
Providing a newsletter signup in the footer as a low-commitment conversion touchpoint.
Organizing secondary navigation links (product, company, legal) that don't belong in the primary header.
avoidWhen: Building an application shell footer — use a simpler footer without marketing navigation columns.
The page is a focused conversion page (signup, checkout) where footer distraction should be minimized.
The footer would be the only navigation on a page — pair it with a header navigation instead.
responsiveBehavior: Multi-column footer link grids collapse to a single column or two columns on mobile. Newsletter form fields stack input and button vertically on small screens. Social icons remain in a row at all widths.
accessibility: Wrap the footer in a <footer> element, which is a landmark region accessible to screen reader navigation.
Each column of links should be a <nav> with a descriptive aria-label (e.g., 'Product links').
Newsletter form inputs must have visible labels; social icon links must have aria-label naming the platform.

variants.title: Large with newsletter form
variants.description: Full-featured footer with multiple link columns, a newsletter signup form in the header area, social icons, and copyright row.
accessibility: Newsletter form field must have a linked label; link columns wrapped in <nav> with aria-label.

variants.title: Large with newsletter form (Dark)
variants.description: Large newsletter-footer adapted for dark marketing sites with dark background and light text.
accessibility: All footer text, links, and form fields must meet WCAG AA contrast on dark footer backgrounds.

variants.title: Simple stacked
variants.description: Compact footer with logo, a short link row, social icons, and copyright stacked vertically — for minimal landing pages.
accessibility: Footer landmark and nav landmark must be present; social links have aria-label naming the platform.

variants.title: Simple stacked (Dark)
variants.description: Compact stacked footer adapted for dark marketing pages.
accessibility: Logo alt and link text must meet contrast requirements on dark footer backgrounds.

variants.title: Simple row
variants.description: Minimal single-row footer with logo on the left, navigation links in the center, and copyright on the right — for SaaS apps and simple product sites.
accessibility: Single-row footer collapses gracefully on mobile; <footer> landmark wraps the entire element.

variants.title: Simple row (Dark)
variants.description: Single-row minimal footer adapted for dark marketing and application surfaces.
accessibility: Link and copyright text must meet contrast requirements on dark footer backgrounds.

variants.title: Call to action with gradient
variants.description: Footer with a bold gradient CTA section above the standard links row — for converting visitors at the bottom of the page before they leave.
accessibility: CTA button on gradient background must meet WCAG AA contrast; gradient must not reduce text legibility.

variants.title: Call to action with gradient (Dark)
variants.description: Gradient-CTA footer adapted for dark marketing sites.
accessibility: Gradient CTA and surrounding dark footer text must all meet contrast requirements.

variants.title: Split with company info, links and image
variants.description: Two-column footer with company description and branding image on one side and navigation columns on the other.
accessibility: Company image must have descriptive or empty alt text; link columns each have a descriptive aria-label.

variants.title: Split with company info, links and image (Dark)
variants.description: Split company-info-and-links footer adapted for dark marketing sites.
accessibility: All link columns and company description text must meet contrast requirements on dark footer backgrounds.

variants.title: Split with company info, links and call to action
variants.description: Two-column footer with company description on the left and navigation columns plus a CTA button on the right.
accessibility: CTA button has a descriptive label; company description and links have sufficient contrast.

variants.title: Split with company info, links and call to action (Dark)
variants.description: Company-info-plus-CTA split footer adapted for dark marketing sites.
accessibility: CTA button and footer link text must meet contrast requirements on dark backgrounds.

variants.title: Newsletter form as priority
variants.description: Footer where the primary visual element is a large newsletter signup form with the navigation links below it — maximizes email capture at page bottom.
accessibility: Newsletter form must have a visible label for the email input; submit button label describes the action.

variants.title: Newsletter form as priority (Dark)
variants.description: Newsletter-first footer adapted for dark marketing sites.
accessibility: Email input and subscribe button must meet contrast requirements on dark footer backgrounds.

variants.title: Centered with branding
variants.description: Centered footer with logo, tagline, social icons, navigation links, and copyright — a clean, symmetrical style for brand-forward marketing sites.
accessibility: Logo alt text names the company; social icon links have aria-label for each platform.

variants.title: Centered with branding (Dark)
variants.description: Centered branding footer adapted for dark marketing pages.
accessibility: Logo, social icons, and navigation links must meet contrast requirements on dark centered footer backgrounds.

variants.title: Slim with branding and link top
variants.description: Very compact footer with minimal branding and a single 'Back to top' link — for long-form marketing articles and blog posts.
accessibility: 'Back to top' link must move focus to the top of the page or a skip-link target, not just scroll.

variants.title: Slim with branding and link top (Dark)
variants.description: Slim compact footer adapted for dark marketing page surfaces.
accessibility: Link text and branding must meet contrast requirements on dark footer backgrounds.

variants.title: Company info and links
variants.description: Footer combining company logo, short description, contact information, and multi-column link navigation — a comprehensive marketing footer.
accessibility: Contact information (phone, address) uses semantic microdata or <address> element where appropriate.

variants.title: Company info and links (Dark)
variants.description: Company info and link-columns footer adapted for dark marketing sites.
accessibility: Company info text and all link columns must meet WCAG AA contrast on dark footer backgrounds.

variants.title: Inline with logo and copyright
variants.description: Minimal single-row inline footer with logo and copyright on the same line — the simplest footer for single-page apps and focused landing pages.
accessibility: Logo alt text names the company; copyright text meets contrast requirements.

variants.title: Inline with logo and copyright (Dark)
variants.description: Minimal inline logo-and-copyright footer adapted for dark surfaces.
accessibility: Logo alt and copyright text must meet contrast requirements on dark footer backgrounds.

variants.title: With call to action
variants.description: Footer with a prominent CTA block at the top (headline, description, and button) above the standard link columns and copyright — for maximizing conversion at page end.
accessibility: CTA button has a descriptive label; footer CTA and navigation sections are distinct landmark regions.

variants.title: With call to action (Dark)
variants.description: CTA-topped footer adapted for dark marketing sites.
accessibility: CTA button and surrounding footer text must meet contrast requirements on dark backgrounds.
